items.author: CoinMarketCap
items.context: @CoinMarketCap (7.071.958 seguidores), en inglés, noticia recién publicada: «Grayscale says this is now Bitcoin's longest bear market on record after BTC fell to $55K but also the shallowest, lasting at least 411 days but with only a 56% drawdown.» Encontrado con minutos de vida y 0 respuestas: ventana para ser de las primeras respuestas. Ángulo: caídas y ciclos, comparando profundidad y duración con los datos del Cycle Clock (2011: −92,7% y 622 días; 2013: −84,5% y 1.177 días).
items.suggested_text:
Both can be true at once, and it's the combination that's new. Earlier cycles were defined by depth: 2011 fell −92.7% and took 622 days to reclaim its high; 2013 fell −84.5% and needed 1,177 days. A −56% drawdown stretched over 411+ days is a different shape: less capitulation, more slow grind.

That fits a maturing asset. Deeper liquidity and a bigger base of long-term holders absorb more of the selling, so the pain shows up in duration rather than in percentage.

Which leaves the part no chart answers yet: does a shallower fall buy a shorter road back to the high, or does the market just charge the difference in time?
